item.research_question: What are the temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy additively manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM), and how do they correlate with the unique microstructure formed during the process?
item.processing_route: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) using pre-alloyed spherical powder (average diameter 27.2 µm); Laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern, high-purity Ar atmosphere.
item.test_conditions: Compression tests performed at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C; initial strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; engineering strain limit 0.4; specimens preheated at 10 °C/min; MoS₂ spray used as lubricant.
key_findings: SLM-built HEA exhibited a yield strength of 778.4 MPa at room temperature, significantly higher than annealed (254.2 MPa) and other AM-processed (approx. 519 MPa) variants.
The average dislocation density was measured at 1.88 × 10¹⁴ m⁻², which is higher than in homogenized HEA.
Nano-sized Mn₂O₃ precipitates with an average size of 27.3 nm were identified at cell structure boundaries.
Average grain sizes varied by direction: 5.98 µm (Building Direction), 12.93 µm (Transverse Direction), and 15.66 µm (Scanning Direction).
Type-C serration occurred at 600 °C with a stress drop amplitude (∆σ) of approximately 4.5 MPa.
Activation energy for deformation at 600 °C was measured at 335 kJ/mol, indicating cooperative lattice diffusion rather than interstitial solute diffusion.
Work hardening occurred from room temperature to 600 °C, while work softening occurred at temperatures higher than 700 °C due to dynamic recrystallization.
Ultra-fine recrystallized grains with an average size of 378 nm were observed at grain boundaries after deformation at 700 °C.
item.mechanism: Superior mechanical properties at low temperatures (25–600 °C) are attributed to fine grain size, high dislocation density, and nano-sized Mn₂O₃ precipitates providing dislocation forest hardening and Orowan strengthening. At high temperatures (≥700 °C), dislocation forest hardening and Orowan strengthening remain dominant as matrix and grain boundary strengthening diminish. Deformation mechanisms shift from slip and deformation twinning (25–600 °C) to slip and partial dynamic recrystallization (≥700 °C). The delay in full recrystallization and strain softening up to 900 °C is caused by the Zener drag effect from Mn₂O₃ precipitates and retarding pressure from migrated grain boundaries.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that previous studies on AM-processed HEA were limited to fundamental investigations and room temperature properties.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work, but implies the need to further understand the correlations among microstructure, properties, and deformation mechanisms to tune alloys for high-performance applications.
quotes: SLM-built HEA has a higher dislocation density of 1.88 × 1014 m−2 as compared to the homogenized HEA.
Phases with an average size of 27.3 nm formed in the cell structure boundary.
The serrated flow of SLM-built HEA can be uninfluenced by interstitial atoms, and this is related to the cooperative lattice diffusion of constituent elements.
